issue.title: Spec: software factory v0 on chronicle
issue.body:
Map: #1. Decisions: #2, #3, #4, #5, #6. Glossary: CONTEXT.md in this repo.

## Problem Statement

Chi has a queue of well-scoped tickets on chronicle and no time to implement them. Every existing tool either needs a human to merge, runs one agent on one machine, or ignores ticket dependencies. She wants tickets to flow to merged code 24/7 with her time spent only on grilling specs and reading an escalation queue, and she wants proof it is autonomous before trusting it.

## Solution

A factory: reusable GitHub Actions workflows in this repo, vendored from sandcastle's label-driven pipeline and pinned, that a target repo calls with one thin workflow file. A dispatcher moves a ticket in the moment its blockers close. An implementer run produces a draft PR after its own review-and-fix pass. A read-only reviewer emits a verdict as a status check. CI gates (existing checks plus red-green proof and no-skipped-tests) plus the verdict plus GitHub's merge queue auto-merge the PR. Runs that fail the retry cap escalate with a kept branch. Subscription accounts rotate on the runner. An audit agent re-reviews every merged PR for the first 20. Chronicle is the first target repo.

## User Stories

1. As Chi, I want a ticket labeled ready-for-agent with no open blockers to be picked up with no action from me, so that chains flow while I sleep.
2. As Chi, I want a ticket whose blockers are still open to wait, so that work lands in dependency order.
3. As Chi, I want each ticket to become exactly one PR from one run, so that review evidence stays small.
4. As Chi, I want the implementer to run Matt's standards-and-spec review and Anthropic's bugs-and-simplification review and fix findings before opening a PR, so that nothing ships without review-and-fix.
5. As Chi, I want a separate fresh-context reviewer that never edits the branch to tick every acceptance criterion with evidence, so that the maker never grades its own work.
6. As Chi, I want the reviewer's pass or fail to be a required status check, so that merge is mechanical.
7. As Chi, I want a PR to fail the gate if its new tests do not fail on main and pass on the branch, so that stubs cannot merge.
8. As Chi, I want a PR to fail the gate if it deletes a test file or adds a skipped, only, or todo test, so that tests cannot be silenced.
9. As Chi, I want the target repo's existing required checks to stay required, so that the factory never weakens what protects main.
10. As Chi, I want auto-merge enabled on every factory PR at creation, so that no human is in the merge path.
11. As Chi, I want the merge queue to rebase and re-test each PR on the latest main, so that ten in-flight PRs do not stall each other.
12. As Chi, I want a run that fails after one automatic retry to leave no PR, label the ticket needs-human, keep its branch, and attach the log, so that my only queue is escalations.
13. As Chi, I want the retry to receive the CI log from the failed attempt, so that the second try is informed.
14. As Chi, I want each run capped at 60 minutes and a turn limit, so that a stuck agent cannot burn a window.
15. As Chi, I want a configurable cap on runs in flight per account (default 3), so that one account is not rate-starved and I can raise the cap from usage data without a code change.
16. As Chi, I want the runner to pick the account with the most remaining quota before each run (or the earliest reset if all are spent) and retry once with the next account on a rate limit, so that a spent 5-hour window does not produce noise escalations.
17. As Chi, I want to add an account by adding one secret, so that scaling is trivial.
18. As Chi, I want an audit agent using the strongest configured model to re-review each of the first 20 merged PRs against its ticket within an hour of merge, so that auto-merge from day one is survivable.
19. As Chi, I want an audit miss to open a revert PR and a needs-human issue, so that a bad merge is contained without me.
20. As Chi, I want the implementer, reviewer, and audit models to be set once per repo as defaults, and overridable per ticket with a model label, so that a hard ticket can get a stronger implementer than a trivial one.
21. As Chi, I want ready-for-agent to remain the human intent label and agent:* labels to be factory state, so that my existing skills keep working unchanged.
22. As Chi, I want sub-issues of a spec to be accepted as tickets, so that /to-tickets output is picked up as is.
23. As Chi, I want the factory prompts to obey the target repo's CLAUDE.md and CONTEXT.md, so that one generic prompt serves every repo.
24. As Chi, I want a target repo onboarded by adding one workflow file and a few secrets, so that Kite repos can follow later.
25. As Chi, I want the agent step to remain swappable to Codex, Pi, or Cursor through sandcastle's agent registry, so that I am not locked to one vendor.
26. As Chi, I want an end-to-end proof run on a fixture repo with seven tickets in two independent dependency chains and a forced rate limit, so that autonomy, dependency order, parallelism, and rotation are demonstrated before chronicle is touched.
27. As Chi, I want every run's token usage recorded per PR, so that cost per merged PR is known.
28. As Chi, I want the factory to refuse tickets labeled ready-for-human or needs-triage, so that human work is never automated by accident.
29. As Chi, I want a ticket that removes a feature to say so in its body and have the gate honour that, so that removals are not blocked by rules written for additions.
30. As Chi, I want a whole spec's sub-issues worked as one run per ticket in fresh sessions, parallel wherever the blocking edges allow, so that onboarding chronicle is a real proof of the loop, not a batch job.

## Implementation Decisions

- Engine: sandcastle's GitHub Actions dogfood pipeline, copied into this repo: the shared, implement, review, and implement-pr scripts, their prompts, and their three workflows. update-branch, explore, the planner prompts, the Dockerfile, and the repo's self-build step are not copied. The library comes from npm pinned to 0.12.0 (which is the repo HEAD) with a lockfile and a committed tarball. The factory's contract with the library is five names: run, the Claude provider, the no-sandbox provider, structured output, and the run types; the agent and sandbox swap surface is those three run calls. Treated as vendored code: edited freely, never upgraded automatically. Known library gaps handled in tickets: no flag passthrough for a turn cap (wrapper provider), the error flag dropped from parsed results (read raw result events via file logging), reviewer prompt edits and pushes (replaced).
- Packaging: reusable workflows in this repo, called from a single factory workflow file in each target repo with the target's secrets passed through. Chronicle first.
- Isolation is GitHub's ephemeral runner; sandcastle's no-sandbox provider. Pushes use a personal access token secret so CI fires on agent pushes.
- Dispatcher: a workflow on issue closed, labeled, and a schedule fallback. Reads open issues carrying ready-for-agent with zero open blockers via GitHub native dependencies and no assignee, adds agent:implement. Refuses ready-for-human and needs-triage. The sub-issue refusal in the vendored implement workflow is removed. The schedule job is also a reconciler (#35): every sweep reads real state and repairs anything past its deadline (a labeled ticket with no run, a PR with no verdict, a cancelled slot run), and it runs on repository_dispatch so it does not depend on GitHub's cron, which slept for seven hours on the fixture on 2026-09-07.
- Implementer prompt: read the ticket, parent spec, and the repo's own docs; TDD at the seams; run mattpocock-skills:code-review and fix all findings; run the bundled code-review with fix; typecheck and full test suite; commit; never push, label, or open PRs (the workflow does). Explicit anti-placeholder rule. Turn cap passed to the CLI.
- Reviewer: fresh context, read-only, receives the ticket's acceptance criteria, the diff, and the red-green output. Outputs a checklist with evidence per criterion and a verdict. The workflow posts the checklist as the PR body section and a status check named factory/verdict. Reject reopens the implementer once with the review, then escalates.
- Gate: target repo's existing required checks unchanged, plus two new required checks provided by the factory: factory/red-green (checks out new or changed test files against main, expects failure; against the branch, expects pass) and factory/test-integrity (diff contains no deleted test files and no new skip, only, or todo markers). Removal tickets: a ticket body with a `## Removes` section listing what is deleted may delete the listed subjects' test files, and red-green passes vacuously when no tests changed; the reviewer verifies each deleted test maps to a listed removal. No section, strict gate. No global label.
- Merge: auto-merge enabled on the PR at creation via the GitHub API; the target repo's main uses a merge queue with strict up-to-date checks. No merger agent.
- Escalation: after one retry the workflow removes agent labels, adds needs-human, comments with the log link, keeps the branch, opens no PR.
- Rotation: one secret per account (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_n), accounts in distinct orgs. A small rotation module with two functions, pickToken and isRateLimited. pickToken(tokens, headroom?) takes headroom as an optional injected input and never fetches it: Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint requires the user:profile scope, which setup-token tokens do not carry (verified 403 oauth_scope_insufficient against all three real tokens on 2026-09-07), so v0 rotation is rate-limit driven. With no headroom, pickToken orders tokens by configured index and skips tokens already known rate-limited in this job. isRateLimited reads the run's JSON result (error flag plus status), never the exit code, since claude -p exits 0 on a rate limit. On a rate limit the job re-runs once with the next token. Each token gets its own config dir and API-key env vars unset. claude-swap's ranking is the reference for the deferred headroom feed (#24), not a dependency. Concurrency: a per-account cap implemented as N named slots (account-<n>-slot-<i>), exposed as a workflow input with a default of 3. GitHub's concurrency key cannot express max-N (one running plus one pending per group), so slots are the mechanism and raising the cap is lengthening a matrix. The cap is load-bearing in v0 since, without headroom ranking, it plus the rate-limit fallback is the only thing spreading load across accounts; set it from the per-PR usage data collected by the audit ticket rather than by guess.
- Audit: a workflow on PR merged; for the first 20 merges (count kept in the state file) runs the reviewer prompt in audit mode with the strongest configured model; a miss opens a revert PR and a needs-human issue.
- Models: implementer, reviewer, and audit models are inputs to the reusable workflow with per-repo defaults. A model label on a ticket (for example model:opus) overrides the implementer model for that run only. Agent choice uses sandcastle's registry.
- Usage: sandcastle's per-iteration usage is written into the PR as a comment.
- Labels created on onboarding: agent:implement, agent:in-progress, agent:review, agent:blocked, needs-human.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test observes external behavior: labels, PRs, checks, merges, and escalations on a repo, or the return value of a pure function. Never the prompt text or workflow internals.
- Top seam, the proof run: a fixture repo on GitHub seeded with a tiny Node project and seven tickets in two independent dependency chains: chain A of four implementable tickets, chain B of three where the middle ticket is unimplementable by design. Run with two accounts and one forced rate limit. Pass means: exactly five PRs merged with no human action (all of chain A plus the first of chain B); within each chain, merges land in dependency order; the heads of both chains ran concurrently (overlapping run timestamps); the unimplementable ticket escalated with a kept branch and no PR; the last ticket of chain B never started; the run finished on the second token after the forced rate limit. This is the acceptance test for the whole spec and runs before chronicle is onboarded.
- Script seams, unit tests with node --test as in chronicle: dispatcher selection (issues plus dependencies in, labels out), rotation (usage responses in, token out; result JSON in, rate-limited or not), red-green checker (two test results in, verdict out), test-integrity checker (diff in, verdict out). Pure functions over fixtures, no network.
- Prompts and YAML are exercised only through the proof run.
- Prior art: chronicle's node --test suite for the script style; sandcastle's own workflows for the YAML shape.

## Out of Scope

- Telegram notifications and the daily digest.
- Complexity and duplication backpressure.
- The update-branch agent for true conflicts (the merge queue handles the non-conflict case; conflicts escalate in v0). Note 2026-09-07 (#19): revised. Attempt 1 of the proof run stalled at chain A's head because the two concurrent chain heads had each appended to the target's README, so README-style conflicts are routine, not rare. A conflict update-branch cannot resolve is now handed to the implementer (`agent:implement` on the PR; implement-pr merges main into the branch and resolves), and it escalates only if that run fails (the #16 retry path). Software-factory PR #40, ADR 0003 amendment.
- The sampled audit after the first 20 clean merges.
- Swapping the agent step to vendor-native actions.
- Kite repos as targets.
- Any planner that invents work.
- API-key billing.
- Quota-aware account ranking (headroom feed for pickToken): #24. v0 rotation is rate-limit driven; the OAuth usage endpoint needs a scope `setup-token` tokens do not carry. See the 2026-09-07 amendment to ADR 0004.

## Further Notes

- Subscription-token use through sandcastle's CLI wrapper is a gray zone under Anthropic's terms; accepted knowingly, with the vendor-native swap as the fallback ticket.
- Chronicle's main already requires check, e2e, and gitleaks; the factory adds factory/verdict, factory/red-green, and factory/test-integrity and turns on the merge queue.
- The 29 existing ready-for-agent issues on chronicle need the ticket template applied before onboarding (map ticket #7).
- Cost, checked 2026-09-07: GitHub Pro, 3,000 included private-repo minutes per month, Linux 2-core at $0.006 per minute. Chronicle is public, so standard runners there are free and unlimited and reusable-workflow minutes bill to the caller; steady state on chronicle costs nothing. The build phase (#10 to #19) runs in the private fixture and this repo, estimated 2,000 to 5,000 minutes total, so $0 to about $42 in overage. A product-level Actions budget of $100 is set on the account with "Stop usage when budget limit is reached" enabled: if private-repo Actions stop abruptly mid proof run, check the budget before debugging the factory.
- Research behind these choices lives as comments on the map's research tickets: #3 (sandcastle and peers), #4 (loops, graphs, Grok Bot vs Ralph), #21 (sandcastle inventory), plus the original market scan attached as a comment on the map (#1).

issue.title: feat/35 reconciler
issue.body:
- **Reconciler: repair stuck factory states on every sweep (#35)**
- **README: the reconciler and the factory-sweep external trigger (#35)**

body:
Merged in #38 (main bc10c3c, 8c209aa). Proven on chizhangucb/factory-fixture with the caller on feat/35-reconciler, deadlines stuck_minutes 5 and verdict_minutes 10 (defaults 15, 30, 30), and a proof knob in the caller that skipped the implement job for issue #62 (simulating the lost event twice). GitHub's cron was not used: every sweep was driven by workflow_dispatch or repository_dispatch, trigger noted per line.

- [x] A fixture ticket left in `agent:in-progress` with no run is re-dispatched by the next sweep, and escalated to `needs-human` after the second miss. Issue https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/issues/62, labeled by hand 18:28Z. Sweep 1 (workflow_dispatch) https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/34152571842: `#62 (issue) agent:in-progress since 2026-09-07T18:28:29Z, 12 min ago, deadline 5 min, no implement run: re-add agent:implement (miss 1)`, marker comment posted, labeled event fired (run 34152596874, implement job skipped by the knob). Sweep 2 (repository_dispatch factory-sweep) https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/34153082743: `#62 (issue) agent:implement since 2026-09-07T18:40:47Z, 7 min ago, deadline 5 min, no implement run, second miss: escalate to needs-human`; the issue got `needs-human`, `agent:*` off, and the escalation comment.
- [x] A fixture PR with `agent:review` and no run is re-reviewed by the next sweep. PR https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/pull/63, labeled 18:28Z with the review job skipped (run 34151782821, every job skipped). Sweep 1: `#63 (pr) agent:review since 2026-09-07T18:28:38Z, 12 min ago, deadline 5 min, no review run: re-add agent:review (miss 1)`; a real review run started, https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/34152605915 (`review / review` in_progress), cancelled by me for budget.
- [x] A fixture PR with auto-merge armed and no verdict past the deadline gets a review run from the sweep. PR https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/pull/64, auto-merge SQUASH, no labels, head 3e18227 at 18:28Z. Sweep 1: `#64 (pr) auto-merge armed, no factory/verdict on 3e18227 since 2026-09-07T18:28:41Z, 11 min ago, deadline 10 min: add agent:review`; review run https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/34152600997 ran to completion and posted `factory/verdict=failure: no acceptance criteria on the ticket` (no linked ticket, as expected; the #16 handler then escalated and closed it).
- [x] A sweep over a healthy fixture makes no changes, and running it twice in a row makes none. After cleanup, workflow_dispatch https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/34153163571 and https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/34153194275, 27 seconds apart, both `0 decision(s), 0 repair(s), 0 applied, 0 failed`.
- [x] The decision function has node --test unit tests over fixture states, no network. `factory/dispatch/reconcile.test.ts`, 32 tests over snapshot fixtures (lost event, second miss, older mark, live and queued runs, dispatch run on the same title, cancelled by slot contention, settling run, parked labels, PR review and implement-pr states, verdict deadline, update-branch window, log line shape, GitHub shape mappers). CI on #38 green.
- [x] The sweep runs on `repository_dispatch` from outside GitHub, proven with one call from a local machine. `gh api repos/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/dispatches -f event_type=factory-sweep` from Chis-Mac-mini at 18:47:55Z produced run https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/34153082743 (event repository_dispatch, title factory-sweep), the one that escalated #62. Documented in README (Dispatcher) and examples/factory.yml.
- [x] Every repair is a logged decision naming the state, the deadline, and the action. Lines quoted above, one per candidate, plus `Applied:` echoes and a summary; sweep.json is uploaded in the run artifact.

Cleanup: #62 closed, #63 and #64 closed with labels removed, proof branches deleted, proof variables deleted, fixture caller back on @main with the factory-sweep type and no knobs.

<!-- factory:sweep miss=1 -->
Reconciler: `agent:implement` since 2026-09-07T18:50:00Z, no implement run after the 15 min deadline. Re-added `agent:implement`. Miss 1 of 2: a second miss escalates to `needs-human`.

Sweep: https://github.com/chizhangucb/factory-fixture/actions/runs/1
